subject.title: [Bug]: Bootstrap files in agentDir are silently ignored — only workspace directory files are injected into system prompt

question: Should OpenClaw keep bootstrap prompt authority limited to workspace files and warn on bootstrap-named files in agentDir, or should explicitly configured agentDir files merge with or override workspace bootstrap files?
rationale: This is a real security/session-state bug, but the permanent fix changes whether agentDir is only runtime/auth state or also a prompt-authority location; the three open closing PRs already encode competing policies.

options.title: Warn and document agentDir state-only
options.body: Land a diagnostic and docs fix that alerts users when bootstrap-named files are found under agentDir while keeping prompt injection anchored to workspace files.

options.title: Load explicit agentDir bootstrap
options.body: Accept agentDir as a prompt source for explicitly configured agents and require compatibility/security proof across CLI, embedded, compaction, and lightweight bootstrap paths.

options.title: Defer for broader context design
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide the larger agentDir/workspace/context-engine ownership model, then close or consolidate the linked PRs accordingly.

recommendation.title: Warn and document agentDir state-only
recommendation.body: Land a diagnostic and docs fix that alerts users when bootstrap-named files are found under agentDir while keeping prompt injection anchored to workspace files.

likelyOwner.reason: The current bootstrap/context source restoration and nearby agent runtime history point to Peter Steinberger as the clearest routing owner for the product boundary decision.
